document.abstract: In moving to a SMPTE ST 2110 IP platform and the very application-specific benefits such as end-point scale, format agnosticism, flexibility, and ease of integration into wider IP/software workflows that such a move brings to live production, it becomes apparent that full use is not being made of the other benefits that can come in transitioning to an IP-based platform. This article examines some of the technologies and working practices that are used by many mainstream IP adopters—enterprises and cloud providers—and outlines a route for improving the systemization of SMPTE ST 2110 live production environments. When adopted, such improvements can lead to faster network creation, easier facility updates and changes, and greater visibility of the benefits that accrue with such technology.

authors.bio: Gerard Phillips is a systems engineer at Arista Networks, a role which involves providing deep technical and architectural support to customers during the design, installation and running of complex IP infrastructure. Before joining Arista five years ago, he spent 22 years at the cutting edge of broadcast technology development with Snell and Wilcox, Snell and finally SAM. His experience ranges from designing composite decoders, deinterlacers, motion compensated standards converters through to helping to shape the company’s IP strategy—you’ll find Gerard listed as one of the contributors to the VSF’s TR-03, much of which eventually became ST-2110. He was an AMWA board member for SAM, and now fulfils that role for Arista Networks.
